ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A student designed a device to measure the magnetic induction strength of a magnetic field. The device consists of a metal rod ab with a mass of $0.2\mathrm{kg}$, a length of $20\mathrm{cm}$, and a resistance of 2Ω. The rod is horizontally suspended by two identical light springs in a uniform magnetic field perpendicular to the plane of the paper and pointing outward. Each spring has a stiffness coefficient of $50\mathrm{N/m}$, with the upper end fixed and the lower end insulated from the metal rod. The metal rod is connected via a switch to a battery with an electromotive force of $12\mathrm{V}$ and an internal resistance of 1Ω. When the switch is open, the system is in a static state; when the switch is closed, the system returns to a static state, and the elongation of each spring changes by $0.2\mathrm{cm}$ compared to when the switch is open. The gravitational acceleration is taken as $10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$.

1. After closing the switch, what is the current through the metal rod?
2. What is the magnitude of the magnetic induction of the magnetic field to be measured?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description first: The attached diagram shows a horizontal metal rod labeled a on the left and b on the right. It is suspended from two vertical springs fixed to a support above. Around the rod there are dots representing a uniform magnetic field coming out of the page, and the field region is labeled B. The two ends of the rod are connected by wires to a lower circuit containing a battery and an open switch in series. Reasoning: When the switch is closed, the circuit resistance is the rod resistance plus the battery internal resistance: R_total = 2 Ω + 1 Ω = 3 Ω. Therefore the current through the rod is I = E/R_total = 12 V / 3 Ω = 4 A. Compare the two equilibrium states. With the switch open, the rod is balanced by gravity and the two spring forces. With the switch closed, current flows in the rod, so the magnetic field exerts a vertical Ampere force on the rod. The gravitational force is unchanged, so the change in the total spring force equals the magnitude of the magnetic force. Each spring changes elongation by Δx = 0.2 cm = 0.002 m. Thus ΔF_springs = 2kΔx = 2 × 50 N/m × 0.002 m = 0.2 N. This equals BIL. The rod length is L = 20 cm = 0.20 m and I = 4 A, so B = 0.2 /(4 × 0.20) = 0.25 T.
